summary: An Indologist, Mukund Lalji Wadekar served as Officiating Director at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 2002-2008) and the Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (attested 2008). He was also General Editor of Gaekwad's Oriental Series (attested 2008).
Mukund Ram Shastri was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who served as Head Pandit at the Research and Archaeological Department in Jammu and Kashmir, attested in 1911 and 1916-1918.

Mumon Yamada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hanazono University (~1920-1925) and under Seisetsu Seki (~1925-1945). He served as president of Hanazono University (1949-1978), abbot at Shofuku-ji (~1949-1978), and head of the Institute for Zen Studies (1964).

Mun-keat Choong is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Paramadhamma Buddhist Institute, Komazawa University (BA), and the University of Queensland, earning an MA and PhD under Roderick S. Bucknell between 1992 and 1998.

Munenobu Sakurai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1984-1989). He served as assistant professor at Iwate University (~1996-2005) and professor at Tohoku University (~2005).

Muneo Tokunaga was an Indologist who studied at Kyoto University and Harvard University (PhD ~1974-1979). He served as assistant professor at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1981-1989) and as associate professor and professor at Kyoto University (~1989-2009).
Muneyoshi Yanagi was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki (~1904-1910) and at the University of Tokyo (~1910-1913).

Mungunchimeg Batmunkh is a scholar of religious studies, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who earned a Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna under doctoral supervisor Brigitte Marschall (attested 2010).

Munis D. Faruqui is a historian and Indologist. He held appointments at the University of California, Berkeley as professor (~2007) and at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research as Director and Sarah Kailath Chair of India Studies (~2013).

Munish Chandra Joshi was an Indologist and historian who served as Additional Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (~1986-1990) and Member Secretary of the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (~1993-2000).

Linguist and Indologist Murray Barnson Emeneau studied at Dalhousie, Oxford, and Yale (PhD under Franklin Edgerton). He taught Latin at Yale (1926) and served as professor of Sanskrit and linguistics at the University of California, Berkeley (1940-1971).

Musashi Tachikawa studied at Nagoya University and earned his PhD at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. In Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, he held posts at Nagoya University, the National Museum of Ethnology, and Aichi Gakuin University.

Historian and Indologist Muzaffar Alam studied at Jamia Millia Islamia, Aligarh Muslim University, and Jawaharlal Nehru University (doctorate ~1977). He taught at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1973-2001) and became George V. Bobrinskoy Professor at the University of Chicago (~2001).

Myles Dillon was a linguist and Indologist who studied at University College Dublin and under Rudolf Thurneysen, among others. He taught at Trinity College Dublin, University College Dublin, and Wisconsin-Madison, later directing the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies (1960-1968).
Myokyo-ni was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Graz and trained under traditional teacher Soko Morinaga in 1984.
Myōsei Tatsuguchi is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as professor (attested 1987) and professor emeritus (attested 2015) at Ryukoku University.

Mysore Hiriyanna was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies who earned his BA and MA at Madras Christian College. He held posts at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore and served as professor of Sanskrit at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1912-1927).

Mysore Narasimhachar Srinivas was an Indologist who studied at Mysore, Mumbai (PhD under G. S. Ghurye), and Oxford (D.Phil.). He taught at Oxford, Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda, and Delhi University, later chairing the Institute for Social and Economic Change (1972-1979).

Mónika Kiss is a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She pursued PhD studies in Japanese studies at Eötvös Loránd University, studying with advisor Masanori Yamaji (attested 2016) and teachers Robert F. Rhodes and Nozomu Saito.
Indologist N. A. Gore served as librarian at the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1957-1958) and at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University (attested 1967).
